title: Computer Security
headline: Computer Security, taught from the slides up
lead: Each lecture deck is rewritten as a textbook chapter: every bullet expanded, every diagram described, every formula worked through. New lectures get added as the semester moves.

title: Operating Systems
headline: Operating Systems, lectures 1 through 11
lead: Complete exam study notes: every slide expanded into full explanation, with definitions, worked examples, misconceptions, and exam traps marked throughout. Chapters 4–7 carried the midterm; chapters 10–11 were the focus of the cumulative final.

title: Computer Organization & Programming
headline: Computer organization, from the transistor count up
lead: Performance math, number systems, and RISC-V assembly: instruction formats and encoding, bitwise masking, the stack and calling convention, branches and constants, with the exam toolkit at the end.

title: System-Level Programming
headline: System-level programming: UNIX and C
lead: The command line and Snowball, then C from the ground up: the compilation pipeline, types, I/O and strings, flow control and scope, and arrays, functions, and pointers, with every pitfall the guide flags.
